source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ / Climate Resilient Orange Growing Technique", Nov 2018, 23pp
text:
Planting material is produced by grafting/cutting propagation from healthy, high-yielding mother trees. A scion or cutting is selected from reddish, semi-hardened new growth - not the oldest wood and not the very newest tender growth - and cut to a length of about 50-60 cm.

The cutting is then wrapped (ការចង/ការវេចខ្ចប់) - commonly using a moist rooting medium such as coconut husk, secured in plastic and tied at both ends, similar in principle to the marcotting method used for standard Pursat orange propagation. The wrapped cutting is kept shaded and watered until roots develop, then potted up in a nursery bag to hardened off before being planted in the field.
